fit: historical Parkinsonian tremor, injected drug and carrier
assessment: At least eight of eleven historical Parkinsonian cases had tremor. Injected drug in oil and wax and oral belladonna lowered amplitude without materially changing incidence or rate. No oil-only exposure. The 1951 Ebin review is the same study family.

fit: early curare suspension, mixed clinical population and indication
assessment: The 200-person clinical series covered several diagnoses. The author describes possible relief of painful rigidity with the injected drug and gives no individual tremor estimate or oil-only comparison.

fit: injected carrier with dyskinesia and motor findings
assessment: Three of six animals received the drug dissolved in injected peanut oil. The reported effect is on levodopa-induced dyskinesia. Rest tremor appears in model description without an oil-only contrast.

fit: shared peanut oil diets and motor proxy assays
assessment: Both diets contained peanut oil. The low rod yielded longer retention under the low-alpha-linolenic acid diet, the high rod and traction comparisons were inconclusive or unchanged, and some learning measures were weaker. No resting-tremor assessment.
The peanut-plus-rapeseed blend was the comparison for salmon-palm oil, with several dietary fatty acids changing. The fish-oil blend reduced general activity or changed habituation.

fit: oral crude-versus-refined peanut oil allergy safety
assessment: Six of sixty participants with peanut allergy reported reactions after crude oil, including two observable or measurable reactions. None reacted after the refined oil. Outcomes are acute allergy signs, with no identifiable rest-tremor response.

fit: oral dietary oil and same-cohort activity report
assessment: One assigned dietary trial with eight weeks of peanut, olive, safflower oil or no study oil in healthy adults. Its companion paper reports no significant change in general activity, and neither report assessed tremor.

fit: cold-pressed edible-oil composition and cell-free assay
assessment: Measured fatty acids, tocopherols and phytosterols in specified cold-pressed oil. Availability of measured composition supplies no observed symptom contrast.

fit: traditional peanut-oil massage for infantile paralysis
assessment: The table associates peanut-oil massage with infantile paralysis. This row identifies no direct witness, measured response or comparable oral route.

fit: traditional culinary and topical oil uses
assessment: Table 2 records customary cooking and topical uses. Study citation counts measure use reports and cannot establish response or clinical effect.

fit: bundled seed extract in chlorpromazine motor model
assessment: The combined methanolic almond, peanut and watermelon seed extract favored less block catalepsy and greater activity. It did not test peanut oil, an isolated seed arm or a resting-tremor outcome.

fit: peanut-oil-based spread and cognitive or mood outcomes
assessment: The main report identifies oil-based control spread in healthy adults and tests cognition, stress and mood. Registration and later companion outcomes belong to the same intervention. No distinct oil-free comparator or tremor endpoint.

fit: oral peanut-oil comparison and sarcopenia outcomes
assessment: The ENHANce trial and nested TEMPUS-FUGIT use a peanut-oil omega-3 placebo in older adults with sarcopenia. The protocol and feasibility report address physical function, and the family has no separate Parkinson tremor result.

fit: groundnut oil in human meals, fasting glucose and lipids
assessment: Metformin-treated outpatients consumed dietary oils including groundnut. The reported glucose and lipid outcomes do not record tremor or an acute hypoglycemic movement phenotype.

Ebin summarizes the same Bird and Meyers comparison. The recovered primary observes a lower tremor amplitude but no frequency or incidence change under the drug treatments. Treat the review as a companion and do not count it independently.
